correctness.rationale: For four-term exclusion, \(b(4n)=b(n)\), \(b(2n+1)=b(n)\), \(b(4n+2)=0\) give a well-founded descent on the positive difference; odd differences meet residue 2 mod 4 and even differences reduce by 2 or 4. For the exact triple census, the constructed 10-state carry machine is exhaustive, and every state has a fully stated transition; the displayed degree-six denominator P and ten H_i polynomials satisfy \((I-zM)H=P f\) coefficientwise. Formal invertibility of I-zM proves the rational function for every L. An integer-only standalone checker reconstructs the reachable graph, checks the symbolic polynomial identity, and cross-checks direct finite counts; all 90102 assertions passed. The initial convention b(0)=1, bound a+2d<2^L and d>0 are explicit. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The support of the classical Baum–Sweet automatic sequence is sparse, with Fibonacci-size dyadic sections. Its additive complexity is mathematically motivated by prior exact sumset questions; an entire progression-length classification and a rational all-depth census of the extremal surviving length-3 patterns refine existence to enumerative structure. The positive-dimensional sparse support surprisingly permits infinitely many triples but no quadruples, while \(T_L\) grows nontrivially across all dyadic depths. This is a natural complete classification with nontrivial carry-state certificate, not an arbitrary bounded computation or relabeling of a known table.
